dedupe_keys.name: international database idb world population estimates and projections

description: The International Database (IDB) of the U.S. Census Bureau provides population estimates and projections for over 200 countries and areas with populations of 5,000 or more, and for thousands of subnational areas. For each country it contains total population, population by single year of age and by five-year age group and sex, and demographic indicators on fertility, mortality and migration, from a base year through 2100 for 1 July of each year. The Census Bureau has produced these estimates since the 1960s and, with the United Nations Population Division, is one of the few organisations that regularly estimate and project the world's population. The IDB was last updated in December 2025 and the next update is planned for November 2026. Access: the IDB web tool for display and download, and the Census Data API (timeseries/idb/1year and 5year, free key required); free and public domain. Caveats: estimates for countries with old or missing censuses rest on assumptions, and subnational data are not available for every country or year. Simulation uses: population exposure and demand scenarios for infrastructure studies outside the United States, including national demand projections to 2100 and age structures for vulnerability analysis. Related records: U.S. national population projections, IPUMS International census microdata, the Census Bureau's subnational population tables on HDX and gridded population products such as LandScan and GHSL.
